title: Perpendicular Anisotropy and g-Factor of Sputtered Ni Films on Si(111) Studied by Angle-Dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance
authors: Dushyant Singh, Tharundev V, Subha Maity, Subhavenkadesh SS, Vigneshwari SR, Krista R. Khiangte
abstract: Ni films with thicknesses of 312 and 1011\,Å were grown on Si(111) by dc magnetron sputtering at room temperature and studied by atomic force microscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, X-ray reflectivity, magnetometry and angle-dependent ferromagnetic resonance. Both films are polycrystalline fcc Ni with smooth surfaces, a bulk-like (111) lattice spacing and a saturation magnetization of ${\approx}480$\,emu\,cm$^{-3}$, and both are magnetized in plane. The angular dependence of the resonance field, from the film plane to the film normal, is described by a uniaxial anisotropy model with first- and second-order terms. From this model, $g = 2.160\pm0.005$ and $2.101\pm0.014$ and effective perpendicular anisotropies of $(6.0\pm0.4)\times10^{5}$ and $(4.5\pm0.6)\times10^{5}$\,erg\,cm$^{-3}$ were obtained for the thinner and thicker film, respectively. The conventional analysis of only the in-plane and perpendicular resonances gives $g$-factors that are lower by 0.02--0.04. The perpendicular linewidths give upper limits for the Gilbert damping of $α\le 0.030$ and $\le 0.038$.
summary: This experimental study investigates the magnetic anisotropy and g-factor of sputtered Ni thin films on Si(111) using angle-dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance. By fitting the resonance field across all angles, the authors determined the perpendicular anisotropy and g-factor for different film thicknesses. The work emphasizes that using the full angular dependence is crucial for accurate magnetic parameter extraction, correcting biases found in simpler measurements.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and the g-factor of sputtered Nickel (Ni) thin films grown on Si(111).
main_result: The full angular dependence analysis provided specific values for the g-factor and perpendicular anisotropies for both thin and thick films, showing discrepancies compared to conventional analysis.
method: Angle-dependent Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) measurements were performed, analyzing the resonance field dependence across various angles using a uniaxial anisotropy model.
model_or_system: The physical system is polycrystalline fcc Ni thin films (312 Å and 1011 Å) sputtered on Si(111). The analysis uses the Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert equation and a free energy density incorporating uniaxial anisotropy terms ($K_1, K_2$).
key_observables: Resonance field ($	ext{H}_R$), linewidth ($\Delta H$), saturation magnetization ($M_s$), g-factor, and effective perpendicular anisotropy ($K_{	ext{eff}}$).

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the field is exactly aligned and that the full angular dependence is necessary to accurately determine magnetic parameters, correcting biases from conventional analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate AFM topography, GIXRD patterns showing crystal structure, and XRR curves confirming film thicknesses. Figure 6 shows the resonance field dependence on the rotation angle for both film thicknesses.
paper_structure: The paper details structural characterization (AFM, GIXRD, XRR) followed by magnetometry and angle-dependent FMR. The core analysis involves fitting the resonance field using a full uniaxial anisotropy model to extract $g$, $M_{	ext{eff}}$, and anisotropy constants, comparing these results against simpler in-plane/perpendicular analyses.
why_interesting: While this is solid-state magnetism, the detailed analysis of magnetic anisotropy and g-factor extraction from resonance spectroscopy is a highly quantitative technique relevant to understanding spin dynamics in nanoscale magnetic systems.
